reproduction.observed: FileNotFoundError [WinError 206] 檔名或副檔名太長 while mkdir on '<dst>\.hgk\rounds\R2-...\openspec\changes\...'
reproduction.first_resolved_path: \c\Users\user\AppData\Local\...\pipd-verify3 (note the literal leading '\c\': the MSYS-style '/c/...' argument was taken as a relative path)

mechanism: dst = Path(args.dst) is used without os.path.abspath/normalisation, so an MSYS-style '/c/...' path resolves as '\c\...' under the current drive and the copy is built in the wrong place; the same deep target then exceeds Windows MAX_PATH and dies with an os-level FileNotFoundError instead of a clear refusal.
impact: A caller following the house habit of MSYS-style paths gets a bogus partial tree and an opaque error; the intended envelope never materialises. No product byte was modified (the failure happened before any write inside --src).
workaround_used: re-run with native Windows paths and a short root: --src C:/Projects/Agent_Workspace/PIPD --dst C:/v3 --scratch C:/w8v3  -> succeeded, copy HEAD 7c5bc585c7d8, dirty 33, equal to source.
fix_recommended: normalise every path argument with os.path.abspath(os.path.expanduser(...)) and reject a path whose resolved form does not sit under the expected drive (or, minimally, warn and refuse when the string starts with '/<letter>/' on Windows)
fail closed with an explicit message when a destination path would exceed MAX_PATH (or enable long-path handling) instead of surfacing the OSError text
add a test: an MSYS-style dst must be either normalised correctly or refused with a named exit code
freeze_note: Recorded during W8-VERIFY-3's freeze window; the artifact was deliberately NOT edited so the verdict's subject stays byte-identical. Repair + narrow delta re-verification to follow the verdict.
